title: Observability dashboards + alerts for PLG signal router (lag, HubSpot failures, task routing volume)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
We have the signal aggregation + HubSpot routing service in flight for the PLG-to-sales pilot. Before we expand cohort/regions we need production-grade observability: a single dashboard AEs/ops can reference for volume + health, plus actionable alerts for the oncall rotation.

This ticket covers:
- Dashboard(s) for pipeline health and throughput
- Alerting for event lag, HubSpot API errors/429s, and task creation anomalies
- Oncall handoff notes/runbook snippets (what to check first, how to backfill/retry)

Why now: We’ve already seen HubSpot 429s during early testing and we need to avoid silent drops/missed follow-up tasks during the NA pilot.
implementation_plan:
1) Define the minimal metric contract we will depend on from the router + aggregator (counters + gauges + timers).
2) Add/confirm instrumentation in signal-router:
   - created_signals (counter)
   - routed_tasks (counter)
   - hubspot_429s (counter)
   - hubspot_5xx (counter)
   - lag_seconds (gauge; end-to-end lag from latest eligible event to routing time)
   - dropped_events (counter; includes validation failures / filtered internal orgs)
   - retry_attempts (counter)
   - queue_depth (gauge) if we’re buffering outbound HubSpot calls
3) Build dashboard:
   - Overview: created_signals, routed_tasks, success rate, top signal types (if tagged)
   - Health: lag_seconds p50/p95, job freshness, error spikes
   - HubSpot: 429s/5xx, request rate, backoff time, task creation success rate
   - Data quality: filtered_internal_orgs count, dedupe rate, suppression hits
4) Create alerts (see Acceptance Criteria) and route to #eng-platform and oncall pager.
5) Document oncall checks + common remediations (HubSpot incident mode, replay/backfill, suppress noisy cohorts).
dashboards:
Primary dashboard name: “PLG Signal Router – Health & Volume”

Suggested layout:
- Top row (KPIs):
  - Routed tasks (last 1h / 24h)
  - Created signals (last 1h / 24h)
  - Task creation success rate
  - End-to-end lag p95 (lag_seconds)

- Pipeline health:
  - lag_seconds timeseries (p50/p95)
  - event ingestion/aggregation freshness (time since last successful aggregation window)
  - dropped_events by reason (validation, denylist/internal, malformed)

- HubSpot integration:
  - hubspot_429s and hubspot_5xx (stacked)
  - HubSpot request count + latency (if available)
  - Retry attempts + backoff duration

- Noise controls:
  - suppression_hits count (signals suppressed due to cooldown)
  - dedupe_hit_rate (if available)

Notes:
- If signal_type is available as a tag/label, include a breakdown table (top 10 signal types in the last 7d) to help PM/Sales quickly see what’s firing.
alerts:
Alert targets (initial thresholds; tune during pilot):

1) End-to-end lag high
- Trigger: lag_seconds p95 > 3600 for 30m
- Severity: page (P1) during pilot hours, otherwise Slack
- Likely causes: aggregator job stalled, queue stuck, HubSpot throttling causing backlog

2) HubSpot rate limit / failure spike
- Trigger: hubspot_429s >= 50 over 15m OR hubspot_5xx >= 10 over 15m
- Severity: Slack + create oncall ticket; page if sustained > 60m
- Likely causes: bursty updates, auth token issues, HubSpot incident

3) Task routing volume anomaly
- Trigger: routed_tasks == 0 for 2h during business hours AND created_signals > 0
- Severity: page (P1)
- Likely causes: router failing to enqueue HubSpot actions, workflow disabled, auth scope revoked

4) Silent drop protection
- Trigger: dropped_events spikes above baseline (e.g., > 5% of created_signals for 1h)
- Severity: Slack
- Likely causes: schema change, validation rules too strict, new internal org patterns

5) Aggregation freshness
- Trigger: time since last successful daily aggregation > 36h
- Severity: Slack, page if > 48h
- Likely causes: warehouse job failure, upstream telemetry lag
acceptance_criteria: A dashboard exists for the signal router that includes created_signals, routed_tasks, hubspot_429s, hubspot_5xx, and lag_seconds (with p50/p95).
At least 4 monitors/alerts are configured: lag, HubSpot failures (429/5xx), routing volume anomaly, aggregation freshness.
Alerts have clear runbook text including first checks and mitigation steps (e.g., enable batching, reduce update rate, pause routing, replay/backfill).
Dashboard link is pinned in #eng-platform and referenced from the oncall handoff doc/thread for the pilot.
Smoke test completed in staging with forced 429s / simulated lag, verifying alert delivery and dashboard correctness.
notes_oncall_runbook:
Oncall quick triage:
1) Check dashboard KPIs: is lag increasing? Are tasks being routed?
2) If hubspot_429s are spiking:
   - Confirm batching/queueing is enabled
   - Reduce concurrency to HubSpot
   - Verify we’re honoring Retry-After and exponential backoff
3) If created_signals > 0 but routed_tasks == 0:
   - Check router deploy status + error logs
   - Confirm HubSpot auth token/scopes are valid
   - Confirm HubSpot workflow is not paused (Ops)
4) If aggregation freshness alert fires:
   - Check daily job status + recent failures
   - Determine whether backfill is needed for missed windows
5) If dropped_events spikes:
   - Pull sample event payloads from logs
   - Compare against schema v1; check for a new enum/value causing validation failures
